controls: A QoS policy applies a Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) value, throttle rate, or both to outbound TCP, UDP, or HTTP response traffic.
4000.title: Policy-based QoS

controls: Only &HTTP server applications responding to requests for this URL:

Example:  http://myhost/training/ or https://*/training/
Example of non-standard TCP port:  http://myhost:8080/training/ or https://myhost:*/training/
4001.title: Policy-based QoS

controls: Specify the source and destination IP addresses.

A QoS policy can be applied to outbound traffic that is from a source or to a destination IP (IPv4 or IPv6) address or prefix. For HTTP response traffic, the destination IP address or prefix denotes the client(s) that issued the HTTP request.
&Only for the following source IP address or prefix:
Onl&y for the following destination IP address or prefix:

Example for a host address: 1.2.3.4 or 3ffe:ffff::1
Example for an address prefix: 192.168.1.0/24 or fe80::1234/48
4002.title: Policy-based QoS

controls: Specify the protocol and port numbers.
A QoS policy can be applied to outbound traffic using a specific protocol, a source port number or range, or a destination port number or range.
&Select the protocol this QoS policy applies to:
F&rom this source port number or range:

Example for a port: 443
Example for a port range: 137:139
T&o this destination port number or range:
4003.title: Policy-based QoS

controls: Manage the throughput of inbound TCP traffic. This setting applies to the entire computer.
4010.title: Inbound TCP Traffic

controls: Use of DSCP markings can be restricted to only QoS policies. This setting applies to the entire computer.
&Control DSCP marking requests from applications and services:
Allow applications and services to set DSCP values independently of QoS policies.
Ignore DSCP marking requests from applications and services. Only QoS policies can specify DSCP values.
4011.title: DSCP Marking Override
